input: Compile a family emergency contact binder

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The range of content (contacts only vs. medical records, insurance, escape plans, etc.) dramatically changes the size and complexity of the binder.
Knowing who is in the household (e.g., young children, elderly relatives, pets) determines which contacts and special information must be included.
Whether it is physical, digital, or both affects format, tools needed, and how it gets stored and accessed during an emergency.
A deadline (e.g., before a trip, hurricane season) sets urgency and affects how thorough the first version needs to be.
Knowing what information has already been gathered vs. what still needs to be sourced determines the immediate first steps.
Understanding who needs to be able to use the binder (e.g., a babysitter, a child, any adult) shapes how it should be organised and labelled.
The level of detail and organisation style (simple one-page sheet vs. tabbed multi-section binder) reflects the user's priorities and how they want it maintained over time.

gold.taskTitle: Compile a family emergency contact binder
gold.taskDescription: Create a physical or digital binder that organises all critical emergency contacts and related information for the family to access quickly in a crisis.

questions.title: Which sections beyond contacts should the binder include?
questions.description: Clarify whether the binder covers only phone contacts or also includes medical records, insurance policies, evacuation routes, financial account info, etc.

questions.title: Who are the household members this binder must cover?
questions.description: Identify all people (and pets) in the household, including ages and any special needs, so the right contacts and information are included for each.

questions.title: Should the binder be physical, digital, or both?
questions.description: Determine the intended format so the correct tools, storage location, and access method can be planned.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or event driving when this needs to be done?
questions.description: Find out if there is a specific date or upcoming event (e.g., travel, severe weather season) that sets a hard completion target.

questions.title: What contact information do you already have gathered?
questions.description: Establish the starting point — what is already collected vs. what still needs to be researched or requested — to determine the immediate first action.

questions.title: Who else needs to be able to use this binder independently?
questions.description: Identify secondary users such as a babysitter, older child, or relative, which shapes how clearly the binder must be labelled and how simple the layout needs to be.

questions.title: Do you want a simple one-page sheet or a detailed tabbed binder?
questions.description: Understand the preferred level of organisation and detail to match the final product to the user's style and how they plan to maintain it going forward.
